newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE TO SUPPORT INTER-BALKAN JOINT VENTURES - MIN.
newsitem.headline: GREECE TO SUPPORT INTER-BALKAN JOINT VENTURES - MIN.

text.p: Greece will support the creation of inter-Balkan joint ventures with headquarters in Greece in an effort to attract investors by offering both low costs and a safe economic environment, the Development Ministry said.

"Special emphasis will be placed on the prospect of joint, transborder or multi-national businesses which have headquarters in our country," Deputy Developement Minister Anna Diamantopoulou told an economic conference.

Companies can keep costs low by locating parts of production in neighbouring countries with small labour costs, while taking advantage of all priviledges of producing in a European Union country, she said.
"Foreign investors can see the rapid improvement of the business climate and infrastructure in Greece in recent years," she said.
"We hope they will create joint ventures with local companies and bring their easternmost businesses to the closest safe environment, Greece."

Apart from such joint ventures, the ministry will also throw its full support behind new energy and technology projects as well as the use of modern financial management techniques, Diamantopoulou said.
One of its prime targets for 1997 will be to finish selling or closing down all remaining debt-ridden state companies, which the ministry hopes to write off by this summer, she added.
The state's new method of supporting companies is through detailed business master plans that emphasise modernisation and employee training.

The ministry's 14 trillion drachma 1994-1999 development budget will select the most environmentally-friendly projects that can boast state of the art technology, she added. --Dina Kyriakidou, Intercontinental Newsroom +301 9206370
